pairs.difference: A: the magnifier's red handle is a fat pill as thick as a sausage, with a domed end, and the steel ring is a heavy round tube. The lens rim is a perfect disc that dominates the card, like a toy. B: the backboard is a flat panel with straight runs and tight bevelled corners, the frame is a thin even rim, and the net strands and pole stay thin.
pairs.fix: Draw a slim magnifier handle about a third of the lens diameter wide, tapering slightly, with a flat end cap. Make the metal rim a narrow flat band, not a thick tube.

pairs.difference: A: the snorkel tube is a thick sausage of even width from the purple tip to the mouthpiece. The mask is a swollen blob whose skirt and frame merge into one rounded mass, and the mouthpiece is a puffy lump at the bottom. B: the caravan body has flat side panels, a straight floor line, and a crisp door and window frames. The tow hitch, jack and step stay thin, and the wheel sits correctly under the body.
pairs.fix: Draw a slim snorkel tube about half the width of the mask strap. Give the mask a flat, narrow frame with a clear rectangular-oval lens and a thin rubber skirt. Make the mouthpiece small and attached to the tube's lower bend.

pairs.difference: B: the zip bag's outline is uneven. Its right edge bulges and steps inward at the lower right, so the bottom corner looks like it is missing a notch, and the film swells into pillowy wrinkles instead of lying flat. A: the racket head is a clean oval with thin strings and a throat of believable width. The grip is a straight cylinder with a flat butt cap, which matches the real cards' simplified true proportions.
pairs.fix: Draw the evidence bag as a flat, thin plastic sleeve: four straight edges, square corners with a slight bevel, and a straight zip strip across the top. Show only a few shallow creases.

pairs.difference: A: this wheel copies the real ship's-wheel card closely, but the eight handles are swollen bowling pins. The rim is a heavy, flat painted ring, and the stand blends into the spokes as one dark mass behind the hub. On the real card, the handles are slimmer turned spindles and the stand sits clearly below the wheel. B: the goal frame is made of thin tubes with tight corner bends, the net is a thin grid, and the floats are straight cylinders.
pairs.fix: Draw slim turned-wood handles with a narrow neck and a small knob tip. Keep the stand as a separate tapered post with a flat plank base, visible below the wheel and not filling the spokes.

pairs.difference: B: the coin-operated viewer is one swollen blob. The eyepiece housing is a fat rounded capsule, the side handle is a thick looped sausage, and the two lenses face the viewer like eyes, which confuses which end is the eyepiece. The body has no flat faces. A: the trench coat has true garment proportions, with a defined collar and lapels, epaulettes, a belt with a knot, turned-back cuffs, and a straight hem. The hanger hook is thin.
pairs.fix: Draw a tower viewer with a boxy binocular head with flat sides and crisp bevelled edges. Put two short eyepiece tubes on the back, a thin side lever, and a slim cylindrical post.

pairs.difference: B: the music player is a swollen pillow. Every face bulges, the corners are soft blobs, and the round button is a puffy dome. A: the camera body is a box with flat front and top faces, straight edges and tight bevelled corners, and its parts read clearly: flash reflector on a thin stalk, viewfinder block, shutter button, and side strap lugs.
pairs.fix: Draw the player as a thin flat slab with straight sides and tight rounded corners. Make it a few millimetres thick, with flat buttons set into the face.

pairs.difference: A: the fan's pleats have uneven widths and its top edge is lumpy. The bottom guard stick is a long plank that sticks out past the leaf, while the matching guard stick on the right side is missing. The pivot is an oversized disc. B: the fedora has a correct pinched crown and a flat band of even width. Its brim is a thin, consistent curve.
pairs.fix: Draw a folding fan with pleats of equal width radiating from a small rivet. Use two matching thin guard sticks that run along both outer edges to the top of the leaf, and give it a smooth arc along the top.

pairs.difference: A: the safe's top surface bulges like a cushion and its top corners are soft blobs. The side walls sag outward, and the feet are short fat stubs. B: the vending machine has flat side and front panels, straight vertical runs and tight bevelled corners. The door frame, slot and handle stay crisp.
pairs.fix: Draw the safe as a hard steel box with flat top and sides, straight edges and small tight bevels on every corner. Use short, narrow, cylindrical feet.

pairs.difference: A: the badge wallet is a flat rectangle with straight edges and small bevelled corners. Its spine is slightly raised, which is plausible for leather. B: the folded map has fold panels and slightly curled paper edges, and the magnifier has a thin handle and a lens rim of believable width. Neither card shows swelling or fattened parts on my vector. A's very straight outline is above the real range on the numbers, but it fits a flat wallet.

B: the sneaker soles are swollen into thick balloon cushions taller than the upper's side panel. The lace loops spill outward in chaotic colored strands that do not line up with the eyelets, and the two shoes merge into one lumpy mass. A: the handcuffs are simplified but read clearly, with two rings, lock blocks and a short chain of thin links.
pairs.fix: Draw running shoes with a midsole about a quarter of the shoe's height. Lace them neatly with one lace running crosswise through a row of evenly spaced eyelets, and show the two shoes as separate shapes with a small gap between them.

pattern: Generated cards still give themselves away by inflation. Panels and slabs (safe, music player, viewer head) swell into pillows with blob corners. Parts that should be thin (handles, tubes, wheel handles) are thickened into sausages or bowling pins. Parts are miscounted or mis-related: an extra or missing guard stick, a lens facing the wrong way, laces that don't meet the eyelets. Real cards keep flat faces, tight bevels and slim functional parts.
